questions.q: The de-Broglie wavelength of an electron is the same as that of a photon. If velocity of electron is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the velocity of light, then the ratio of K.E. of electron and K.E. of photon will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For photon,

EP=hcλp⇒λp=hcEP

For electron

λe=hmeve=hve2 Ke

Given ve=0.25c. So,

λe=h×0.25c2 Ke=hc8 Ke

Also λp=λe. Thus,

hcEp=hc8Ke⇒KeEp=18

questions.q: A metallic surface is illuminated with radiation of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>λ</mi></math>, the stopping potential is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math>. If the same surface is illuminated with radiation of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>λ</mi></math>, the stopping potential becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>. The threshold wavelength for this metallic surface will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the threshold frequency be λ0.

By the equation of photoelectric effect, for wavelength λ,

eV0=hc1λ-1λ0   ...(i)

For the wavelength 2λ,

eV04=hc12λ-1λ0   ...(ii)

Dividing (i) by (ii)

4=hc(λ0-λλλ0)hcλ0-2λ2λλ0⇒4=2(λ0-λ)λ0-2λ⇒2λ0=6λ⇒λ0=3λ

questions.q: The stopping potential in the context of photoelectric effect depends on the following property of incident electromagnetic radiation:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to Einstein’s photoelectric equation, stopping potential depends on frequency as

hν-hν∘=eVV=hν-hν∘e

Hence stopping potential depends on frequency.

questions.q: An electron (mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math>) with an initial velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>v</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is moving in an electric field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>E</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is constant. If at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, de-Broglie wavelength is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></math>, then its de-Broglie wavelength after time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is given by
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initial de-Broglie wavelength of electron,

λ0=hmv0 ....(i)

Force on electron in electric field,

F=-eE=-e-E0i^=eE0i^

Acceleration of electron, a=Fm=eE0i^m
Velocity of electron after time t,

v=v0i^+eE0i^mt=v0+eE0mti^=v01+eE0mv0ti^

de-Broglie wavelength associated with electron at time t is

λ=hmv

⇒λ=hmv01+eE0mv0t=λ01+eE0mv0t

questions.q:
The magnetic field associated with a light wave is given, at the origin, by B=B0 sin⁡3.14×107ct+sin⁡6.28×107ct. If this light falls on a silver plate having a work function of 4.7eV, what will be the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons?

(c=3×108 m s−1,h=6.6×10−34 J s)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
B=B0sin⁡3.14×107ct+sin⁡6.28×107ct

Maximum KE will associate with the maximum frequency

fmax⁡ =6.28×107c2π=107×3×108 Hz           =3×1015 Hz

KEmax=hfmax-ϕ

=6.63×10-34×3×10151.6×10-19-4.7 eV

questions.q:
The electric field at a point associated with a light wave is given by
E=200sin6×1015t+sin9×1015t Vm-1

Given: h=4.14×10-15 eVs

If this light falls on a metal surface having a work function of 2.50 eV, the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: E=200sin6×1015t+sin9×1015t V m-1

Here, angular velocity, ω1=6×1015 and ω2=9×1015

Maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron is KEmax.=E-ϕ

=hf-ϕ=hω2π-ϕ

=4.14×10-15×9×10152×3.14-2.5=5.92-2.50=3.42 eV

questions.solution:

vpvα=mαmp×λαλp

questions.q: The variation of stopping potential V0 as a function of the frequency (ν) of the incident light for a metal is shown in figure. The work function of the surface is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The relation between the stopping potential and the frequency of the incident light is given by

eV0=hν-ϕ   ...1

When V0 = 0,

ϕ=hν   ...2

Substitute the value of the frequency corresponding to zero stopping potential into equation (2) to calculate the required work function of the material.

ϕ=6.626×10-34 J·s×5×1014 Hz1.6×10-19 J/eV=6.626×516≈2.07eV

In a photoelectric effect experiment, the threshold wavelength of light is 380 nm . If the wavelength of incident light is 260 nm , the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons will be
Given E (in  eV ) =1237λ(in nm)

questions.q: A proton of mass ' $m_{\mathrm{p}}$ ' has same energy as that of a photon of wavelength ' $\lambda$ '. If the proton is moving at non-relativistic speed, then ratio of its de Broglie wavelength to the wavelength of photon is.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy of photon $=E=\frac{h c}{\lambda}\Rightarrow$ Wavelength of photon $=\lambda=\frac{h c}{E}$
Energy of proton $=E=\frac{1}{2} m_p v^2=\frac{P^2}{2 m_p}\Rightarrow$ Linear momentum of proton $=P=\sqrt{2 m_p E}$
Or de-Broglie wavelength of proton
$\begin{aligned}
=\lambda_p= & \frac{h}{P}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m_p E}} \\
\text { Ratio } \frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda} & =\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m_p E}} \times \frac{E}{h c} \\
& =\frac{1}{c} \sqrt{\frac{E}{2 m_p}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& (\mathrm{KE})_{\max }=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi \\ & \frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda} \gt \phi[\text { for emission }] \\ & \lambda \lt \frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\phi} \Rightarrow \lambda \lt \frac{1242}{3} \mathrm{~nm}
\end{aligned}$
So blue light option (B)

questions.q:
A proton and an electron are associated with same de-Broglie wavelength. The ratio of their kinetic energies is:
(Assume h=6.63 $\times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~s}, \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}=9.0 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}=1836$ times $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda$ is same for both
$P=\frac{h}{\lambda}$ same for both
$\mathrm{P}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mK}}$
Hence,
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{K} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{~m}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{e}}}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}=\frac{1}{1836}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The threshold frequency of metal is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math>. When the light of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is incident on the metal plate, the maximum velocity of photoelectron is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>. When the frequency of incident radiation is increased to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math>. the maximum velocity of photoelectrons emitted is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. The ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maximum kinetic energy is related to the incident frequency f and the threshold frequency f0 as:

Kmax=hf-hf0

When, f=2f0

12mv12=2hf0-hf0=hf0     ...1

When, f=5f0

12mv22=5hf0-hf0=4hf0    ...2

Hence, the ratio, v1v2=12

λeλp=mpme
=1836 meme

questions.q: Two streams of photons, possessing energies to five and ten times the work function of metal are incident on the metal surface successively. The ratio of the maximum velocities of the photoelectron emitted, in the two cases respectively, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation,

Maximum kinetic energy, KEmax=E-ϕ, where, E is energy of photon and ϕ is work function.

For two cases, 

12mv12=5ϕ-ϕ=4ϕ and 12mv22=10ϕ-ϕ=9ϕ

Thus, the ratio v1v2=49=23=2:3

questions.solution:
As we know, de Broglie wavelength is given by,

λ=hp

Now kinetic energy can be written as,

K=12mv2=p22m=h22mλ2

Therefore,

K∝1m

Hence, required ratio

KpKα=mαmp=4⇒mα:mp=4:1

questions.q:
With reference to the observations in photo-electric effect, identify the correct statements from below:

A. The square of maximum velocity of photoelectrons varies linearly with frequency of incident light.

B. The value of saturation current increases on moving the source of light away from the metal surface.

C. The maximum kinetic energy of photo-electrons decreases on decreasing the power of LED (light emitting diode) source of light.

D. The immediate emission of photo-electrons out of metal surface can not be explained by particle nature of light/electromagnetic waves.
E. Existence of threshold wavelength can not be explained by wave nature of light/electromagnetic waves.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Einstein's photoelectric equation, 

Maximum kinetic energy, KEmax=12mvmax2=hf-ϕ, where, vmax is maximum velocity of photoelectrons, h is Planck's constant, f is frequency of incident light and ϕ is work function of metal.

From above relation, we can see that the square of maximum velocity of photoelectrons varies linearly with frequency of incident light.

If we increase the intensity of the incident radiation by keeping the frequency constant, then the value of saturation current increases in proportion to the intensity of the incident radiation. Thus, saturation current decreases on moving the source of light away from the metal surface.

The kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is directly proportional to the light frequency, and it remains constant as light amplitude or power of source increases.

Photoelectric effect cannot be explained on the basis of wave nature because experimentally a particular energy called the work function of the metal surface in needed to eject electrons from surface, irrespective of the time for which light is incident. 

Photoelectric effect can be explained by particle nature of light (i.e. quantum theory). Threshold wavelength is maximum wavelength at which emission takes place.

questions.q: The kinetic energy of an electron, α-particle and a proton are given as 4K, 2K and K respectively. The de-Broglie wavelength associated with electron (λe), α-particle (λα) and the proton (λp) are as follows:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a particle is given by

λ=h2mK   ...1

Now, the masses of the given particles are interrelated by the following relations:

me≈mp1837mα=4mp

The de Broglie wavelength for electron is given by

λe=h2me4K= h81837mpK   ...2

The de Broglie wavelength for proton is given by

λp=h2mp2K= h4mpK   ...3

And, the de Broglie wavelength of alpha particle is given by

λα=h2mαK= h24mpK= h8mpK   ...4

From equation (2), (3) and (4), it can be concluded that λe>λp>λα.

questions.q:
In photoelectric effect, the stopping potential $\left(\mathrm{V}_0\right) \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s}$ frequency $(\nu)$ curve is plotted.
( h is the Planck's constant and $\phi_0$ is work function of metal )
(A) $\mathrm{V}_0 \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s} \nu$ is linear.
(B) The slope of $\mathrm{V}_0 \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s} \nu$ curve $=\frac{\phi_0}{\mathrm{~h}}$
(C) h constant is related to the slope of $\mathrm{V}_0 \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s} \nu$ line.
(D) The value of electric charge of electron is not required to determine $h$ using the $V_0 \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s} \nu$ curve.
(E) The work function can be estimated without knowing the value of $h$.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{hv}=\phi+\mathrm{KE}_{\max } \\
& \mathrm{KE}_{\max }=\mathrm{eV}_0 \\
& \mathrm{~V}_0=\frac{\mathrm{hv}-\phi}{\mathrm{e}}
\end{aligned}$
(A) $\mathrm{V}_0 \mathrm{v} / \mathrm{s} \mathrm{V}$ is linear correct
(B) Slope
$\mathrm{v}_0=\left(\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{e}}\right) \mathrm{v}-\frac{\phi}{\mathrm{e}} \text { Wrong }$

Slope $\frac{h}{e}$
(C) Correct
(D) Incorrect
(E) Correct
